title: Critics Mocked Side-to-Side Eye Therapy, Yet Brain Recordings Caught It Silencing Fear
description:
Experimental Chronicle — Francine Shapiro (1989) & Jinhee Baek (2019): Bilateral Eye Saccades, Working-Memory Taxing & Fear-Circuit Suppression, grounded in Francine Shapiro (1989) (Journal of Traumatic Stress). Empirical findings show that in May 1987, Francine Shapiro noticed while walking through a California park that disturbing thoughts abruptly lost their emotional charge whenever her eyes darted rapidly back and forth across trees and pathways.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how amygdala, thalamus, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that in 1989, Shapiro published a randomized controlled study of 22 trauma survivors (combat veterans and assault survivors, average symptom duration ~23 years) comparing rhythmic bilateral saccadic eye movements during trauma recall against an exposure-only placebo description condition.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Francine Shapiro (1989). Efficacy of the eye movement desensitization procedure in the treatment of traumatic memories. Journal of Traumatic Stress. https://doi.org/10.1002/jts.2490020207
- Jinhee Baek, Sukchan Lee, Taesup Cho, Seong-Wook Kim et al. (2019). Neural circuits underlying a psychotherapeutic regimen for fear disorders. Nature. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-0931-y
- Jenny Ann Rydberg (2020). Hommage à Francine Shapiro. Journal de l'hypnose et de la santé intégrative. https://doi.org/10.3917/jhsi.010.0110

AI Disclosure: Visual reenactments, 3D anatomical models, and narration in this documentary Short were produced with AI synthesis tools from verified peer-reviewed sources.
